key_insight: Training PV predictors to forecast multiple future time steps at once improves learning of long-term temporal dependencies and boosts accuracy across the whole horizon.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable, low-overhead way to improve solar power forecasting for grid scheduling, dispatch, and stability management.
method: Combine ground-based sky images with historical PV generation data.
Train deep learning models in a multi-horizon setup rather than single-point prediction.
Compare the approach across multiple architectures to test architecture-independent gains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative experiments across diverse deep learning architectures showing better accuracy and robustness over the full forecast horizon with negligible extra computation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and synchronization of image and PV time-series inputs, so deployment needs careful data alignment and sensor reliability checks.
paper_title: Learning Long-Term Temporal Dependencies in Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Through Multi-Horizon Forecasting
